brief: BofA's weekly systematic flows monitor reports model estimates, not a directional call. Estimated CTA equity positioning stayed broadly long, with medium- and long-term trend signals near maximum on every index tracked, so the only week-over-week change was faster models trimming Russell 2000. Because sell triggers sit far from spot, roughly 1.4 percent below in Euro Stoxx 50 up to about 4 percent in Nasdaq-100, and realized volatility is subdued, BofA sees limited risk of broad systematic deleveraging. In rates, US Treasury shorts held near max while rising German yields pushed CTAs to extend Bund shorts. In FX, trend followers sold the dollar and built EUR, GBP and AUD longs. Commodity trends firmed, led by soybeans and soybean meal, with gold's short- and medium-term signals improving even as the longest-horizon models stay short. SPX hedger gamma climbed to $10.9bn, the 94th percentile, after briefly falling to $3.3bn, and next week's four expiries add a combined $3.7bn.
